title: One PLB L6 over lines approved at different times, or attributed again after a later upload; then interest taken back
assertion: Its entries of each sign never sum past what its attribution gives it of that sign (the most any reconcile's attribution of it gave) nor its Postgres bound, however many reconciles run; when a later upload changes whom it is for, what it gave stands and it writes only what is left of that sign (a claim on another case named later gets nothing); whom each PLB L6 is for is read as of one moment, so an upload during a reconcile changes nothing halfway. An entry is flagged allocated only when its amount is one of two or more parts of a pro-rata split. Interest taken back, by a reversal alone, after a restatement, or netted in one PLB L6 with interest paid, is a negative interest entry against the lines holding that claim's interest, split by what each holds, never below zero on a line, and the interest total is net of it; where that PLB L6's interest paid could reach only the lines its interest taken back reaches, the take-back is written and the payment is not, so the figure errs low, never above the cash. Its interest paid waits while the interest it takes back from a claim whose interest may yet arrive on a case line (its reversal linked to no claim yet, or the claim matched to a case line) is not taken back whole, unless the rest is interest other PLB L6s paid that claim that can reach no line, less what other PLB L6s still owe of take-backs of it; for one take-back of a claim, the outcome is then the same whichever remittance is uploaded first, the netting PLB L6 before, between or with the PLB L6s paying that claim's interest, dated before it or after it, while the later payment is split by the same weights in either order or can reach no line (when the claim's lines change weight between the uploads, by a later approval or a recoupment of only some of them, the payment can be split differently and the take-back reach other lines). When two PLB L6s take back one claim's interest and the uploads pay it less than they take back together, which of them is taken back whole, and so whether its interest paid is written, can depend on the order, and the figure errs low either way. Interest paid for a claim never goes to a line on which another PLB L6 still owes a take-back of that claim's interest that it can no longer write there, nor moves to another of the claim's lines for it, so a person who matches the claim to that line by hand afterwards adds nothing. Nor does it go to a line while the line holds interest of another claim that is no correction of it (one the loader links to nothing): one PLB L6 writes one entry on a line, so it could take only one of two such claims' interest back from it; a line holds one such claim's interest at a time, the other's is written once the line holds none, in that reconcile, if its PLB L6 still owes it, and until then the figure errs low, so one PLB L6 taking back both leaves none of either on the lines, never above the cash. Each reconcile walks the PLB L6s again until a walk writes nothing, so it ends where the reconciles after it would: interest paid by a check dated after two take-backs of its claim, landing on a line once one of them is whole, is taken back in the same reconcile, never above the cash until the next; a reconcile whose PLB L6s still write on the last walk the entries they can write allow, which no real ledger reaches, is refused whole and retried, and every other reconcile completes. Postgres refuses an interest match without its PLB L6 and claim, an entry past its PLB L6's bound either way, and a line's interest below zero; it skips the reconcile job's interest match that carries only one of them

The original reversed (paid -106.00) and the correction C (SYNCCNLED240002), 97110 allowed 100.00, PR-2 coinsurance 20.00, paid 80.00, and 97110-59 allowed 100.00, PR-3 copay 20.00, paid 80.00, with AMT I 5.40, and PLB L6 -5.40 naming C: BPR02 59.40.

paired.835's remittance, which the ledger oracle loads after original.835: The original reversed (paid -106.00) and the correction C (SYNCCNLED240002), 97110 allowed 100.00, PR-2 coinsurance 20.00, paid 80.00, and 97110-59 allowed 100.00, PR-3 copay 20.00, paid 80.00, with AMT I 5.40, and PLB L6 -5.40 naming C: BPR02 59.40.

After paired.835: C reversed (paid -160.00, AMT I -5.40) and restated (SYNCCNLED240007) with the same amounts and AMT I 5.40, beside another patient's claim paying 150.00, and no PLB L6: BPR02 150.00.

C (SYNCCNLED240002) alone, under a patient control number of its own (SYNPCNLED24099) and with no REF F8, so the reconcile places it on no case line, paying 160.00 with AMT I 5.40, and a PLB L6 of -5.40 naming it: BPR02 165.40.

The original reversed (paid -106.00) and C1 (SYNCCNLED240022), 97110 allowed 100.00, PR-2 coinsurance 20.00, paid 80.00, and 97110-59 paid as before (allowed 70.00, paid 50.00), with AMT I 1.00, and a PLB L6 of -1.00 naming C1: BPR02 25.00.

scenario.packet: submitted for the 97110 line before the adjusted remittance arrives

approvedLater.note: never split again when line 2 gains an approval: 5.40 on line 1, not 8.40

laterNamedLatest.note: named by F2, the latest correction: credited to line 2, which F2 approved, never split onto line 1 through F1's claim match

bothWays.note: the other claim's 2.00 on no case line

twoChains.note: the take-back is written first on the lines holding C's interest; B's 6.00 would land on the same lines, which hold one entry of each PLB L6, so it is not written: the figure errs low, never above the cash

twoChainsOutOfOrder.note: two-chains.835 first: C's reversal is linked to nothing yet and its take-back finds no line, so B's payment waits and nothing is written; once paired.835 links it and pays C's 5.40 on the lines, the take-back is written there and B's payment is not, as in twoChains

matchedByHand.note: C is on no case line when the PLB L6 netting B's 6.00 paid against C's 5.40 taken back is written, so its take-back finds no line and B's 6.00 goes to both lines; a person then matches C to both lines by hand, and unplaced.835's 5.40 for C never goes to a line on which that PLB L6 still owes C's take-back and can write nothing more: the figure stays the cash, 6.00, never 11.40. Matched by hand before unplaced-two-chains.835 is uploaded (matchedFirst), C's 5.40 is paid and taken back on the lines and B's payment is not written, as in twoChains

partlyTakenBack.note: C's 5.40 is paid on lines 1 and 2 by two PLB L6s and taken back there; the second patient's 6.00, netted against it in one PLB L6, is written on line 3: the figure is the cash

partlyTakenBackBetween.note: netted-elsewhere.835 between them: it takes back the 1.00 on the lines and its payment waits for the 4.40 still owed; rest-paid.835's 4.40 can then go to neither line (the netting PLB L6 has reached both, and C's reversal left nothing remaining on them), so it is interest credited nowhere, the take-back is whole and the second patient's 6.00 is written on line 3, as uploaded in order; the same when netted-elsewhere.835 and rest-paid.835 are uploaded before one reconcile

shortTakenBack.note: C's interest is paid 3.00 and taken back 5.40: the take-back is written as far as the lines hold and the 2.40 more, which may yet arrive, holds the second patient's 6.00 back, so the figure errs low, never above the cash

shortTakenBackOutOfOrder.note: netted-elsewhere.835 first: C's reversal is linked to nothing yet and its take-back finds no line; short-paid.835's 3.00 then reaches no line, since C's reversal, linked once C arrives, leaves nothing remaining on them, and 3.00 is short of the 5.40 taken back: nothing is written, the same figure as uploaded in order

laterPaid.note: C's claims are matched to both lines before any PLB L6 pays its interest, so C may yet hold interest there: as in twoChains, the take-back is written and B's payment is not

laterPaidAfterNetting.note: two-chains.835 before later-paid.835: C, matched to both lines, may yet hold interest there, so the take-back, finding none, holds B's payment back; later-paid.835's 5.40 lands on the lines and is taken back there, and B's payment is not written, as uploaded in order

oneLine.note: C1 approved line 1 alone: its 5.40 is paid there by two PLB L6s and taken back there, and B's 6.00 goes to line 2, which B approved; the same when one-line-netted.835 and one-line-rest-paid.835 are uploaded before one reconcile, the later payment walked first

oneLineBetween.note: one-line-netted.835 between them: it takes back the 1.00 on line 1 and its payment waits; one-line-rest-paid.835's 4.40 belongs on line 1, which C1 approved, where the take-back can write nothing more, so it is written nowhere, never moved to line 2, which C1 left as it was; the take-back is then whole and B's 6.00 goes to line 2, as uploaded in order

oneLineLate.note: one-line-late-paid.835, dated after one-line-netted.835: its 4.40 belongs on line 1, where the netting PLB L6 has written and can write nothing more, so it is written nowhere, the take-back is then whole and B's 6.00 goes to line 2; the same when the two are uploaded before one reconcile, in either order: the netting PLB L6, dated first, is walked first, and once it has written on line 1 the later payment in the same reconcile reads line 1 as out of its reach

takenBackTwice.note: C's 5.40 is paid on lines 1 and 2 by two PLB L6s; netted-first.835 takes 3.00 of it back there, whole, and the second patient's 6.00 it nets is written on line 3; netted-second.835 takes back 4.40, finds the 2.40 left, and the 2.00 more is interest no upload pays, so its 6.00 for the second patient waits for good: the figure errs low, never above the cash

takenBackTwiceRestLast.note: rest-paid.835 last: netted-first.835 takes back the 1.00 on the lines, netted-second.835 finds nothing left, and both wait; rest-paid.835's 4.40 can then go to neither line (netted-first.835 has reached both), so it is interest credited nowhere, and each take-back counts it less what the other still owes (4.40 less 4.40, and 4.40 less 2.00), so neither is whole and neither 6.00 is written: the outcome depends on the order, 0.00 here and 6.00 in date order, and errs low either way, never above the cash. Counted for both, it would credit 12.00

takenBackTwicePaidAfter.note: cent-paid.835's 0.01 lands on line 2 alone and netted-first.835 takes it back there, still owing 2.99, so it keeps C's payments off line 2; netted-second.835 counts paid-after-both.835's 7.50 for line 2 as interest no line can take, less those 2.99, so it is whole and its 6.00 is written, and paid-after-both.835's 6.00 for line 1 lands there. The reconcile walks the PLB L6s again until a walk writes nothing: 2.99 and 3.01 are taken back on line 1, netted-first.835's 6.00 is written, the 7.50 lands on line 2 once netted-first.835 no longer keeps it off, and the 1.39 netted-second.835 still owes is taken back there: 18.11, the cash, when that reconcile ends, uploaded in date order or before one reconcile. Walked once, it would end at 12.00 or 18.00 and the next reconcile at 19.50, above the cash

bothTakenBack.note: both lines hold C's 5.40 when unlinked-paid.835 pays B's 6.00, so B's payment is kept off them and written nowhere: a line holds one chain's interest at a time, because one PLB L6 writes one entry on a line and could not take two chains' interest back from it; both-taken-back.835 then takes C's 5.40 back from the lines and finds none of B's, which was never credited: 0.00 on the lines against 0.00 of cash, where both chains' interest on the lines left 6.00 of B's above it

bothTakenBackUnlinkedFirst.note: unlinked-paid.835 first: B's 6.00 is on the lines, so paired.835's 5.40 for C is the payment kept off them; both-taken-back.835 takes B's 6.00 back there and counts C's 5.40 as interest no line took: the lines differ from bothTakenBack by which chain reached them first, and the figure is the cash either way

bothTakenBackFirst.note: both-taken-back.835 first: its reversals of C and B leave neither line an approval remaining, so the interest paired.835 and unlinked-paid.835 pay afterwards is split over nothing and written nowhere, and the take-backs find none: 0.00 against 0.00 of cash

unlinkedPaidThenTakenBack.note: B's 6.00, kept off the lines while they hold C's 5.40 (the figure 5.40 against 11.40 of cash: low), is written in the reconcile in which taken-back.835 takes C's back: the PLB L6s are walked again, the lines hold none of C's and B's PLB L6 still owes its 6.00, so the figure ends at the cash
